reason: The hypothesis directly restates the mechanism and outcome from P6 and P17, where coherent nanoprecipitates in a tungsten-based HEA are shown to facilitate dislocation glide and delay cracking, leading to high strength and ductility. It applies this exact mechanism to a different alloy (WTaTiVZr) without new justification or integration of other evidence, making it a restatement of a known result as a prediction.
copied_elements: coherent nanoprecipitates facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations (P6, P17)
stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) design concept (P6)
coherent interfaces of nanoprecipitates delay crack initiation (P6, P17)
improved toughness and ductility from nanoprecipitates (P6)
higher activation energy and smaller creep displacement for HEAs vs. pure W (P4, P8, P9)
